content.user_title: Extract Security Requirements From Threat Models
content.value_statement: Threat models often fail to become testable requirements. This skill converts threats, business context, and compliance needs into prioritized security stories.
actual_capabilities: Converts STRIDE threat categories into security requirement patterns.
Creates security user stories with acceptance criteria and test cases.
Prioritizes requirements from threat impact and likelihood.
Maps requirements to compliance frameworks such as PCI DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, and OWASP.
Builds traceability matrices from threats, controls, and requirements.
Highlights gaps in compliance control coverage.
limitations: Requires a threat model or clear business context as input.
Does not verify implemented controls in a live system.
Compliance mappings are examples and need expert review.
Generated requirements may need tuning for local architecture and policy.

use_cases.title: Convert threat models into backlog items
use_cases.description: Turn STRIDE findings into security user stories, priorities, acceptance criteria, and test ideas for delivery teams.

use_cases.title: Define release-ready security acceptance criteria
use_cases.description: Translate business risks into clear requirements that product and engineering teams can estimate and verify.

use_cases.title: Map requirements to compliance controls
use_cases.description: Connect requirements to framework controls and identify weak or missing coverage before an audit.

prompt_templates.title: Extract basic requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to convert these threats into security requirements. For each requirement, include a title, rationale, priority, and acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Create security user stories
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create security user stories from this threat model. Include role, goal, benefit, priority, acceptance criteria, and security test cases.

prompt_templates.title: Map requirements to compliance controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to map these requirements to PCI DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, OWASP, or SOC 2 controls. Identify gaps and weak coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Build a traceable security backlog
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning across threats, controls, and tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to produce a traceable security backlog from the attached threat model and business goals. Group by domain, priority, dependency, compliance mapping, and verification method.

output_examples.input: A spoofing threat affects customer login for a payment application.
output: Requirement: Implement strong authentication for customer login.
Priority: High, because account takeover can expose payment data.
Acceptance criteria: Unauthenticated access is denied, failed logins are logged, and sensitive actions require stronger verification.
Test case: Invalid credentials are rejected and recorded for monitoring.

output_examples.input: A team needs GDPR and OWASP coverage for sensitive profile data.
output: Requirement: Encrypt sensitive profile data at rest and in transit.
Compliance mapping: GDPR Article 32 and OWASP data protection controls.
Gap: Define log redaction rules for profile data access events.

output_examples.input: An API tampering threat targets order update requests.
output: Requirement: Validate every order update request against expected formats and authorization rules.
Acceptance criteria: Malformed input is rejected and unauthorized updates are blocked.
Security test: Tampered order identifiers cannot modify another customer order.

best_practices: Provide concrete threats, affected assets, impact, likelihood, and business goals.
Ask for acceptance criteria and test cases for every generated requirement.
Review compliance mappings with a qualified security or legal expert.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for vague requirements such as make the system secure.
Do not skip traceability between threats, controls, and tests.
Do not treat generated compliance mappings as legal advice.

faq.question: What input works best with this skill?
faq.answer: A threat model with assets, threats, targets, impact, likelihood, and business context works best.

faq.question: Can it create security user stories?
faq.answer: Yes. It can produce user stories with priorities, acceptance criteria, and security test cases.

faq.question: Does it support compliance mapping?
faq.answer: Yes. The playbook includes example mappings for PCI DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, OWASP, and related controls.

faq.question: Can it replace a security review?
faq.answer: No. It helps draft requirements, but experts should review risk, architecture, and compliance decisions.

faq.question: Does it scan systems or run tests?
faq.answer: No. It creates requirements and test ideas, but it does not inspect live systems.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
